D012-D018_h001.question: "It’s gotten to the point where I just can’t deal with anything medical. A few months ago, I was in a bike accident delivering food – just a nasty scrape, but ever since, if I so much as see a band-aid, my heart starts pounding out of my chest, I get all shaky and can barely breathe. Forget about injections, even thinking about a needle makes me dizzy. I ended up with a pretty bad cut on my arm from the accident, but I cleaned it myself and avoided the hospital because the thought of getting stitches or a tetanus shot sent me into a full-blown panic. I haven’t really had flashbacks or nightmares about the crash itself, and I’m back on the bike every day, no problem. It’s just this intense dread around anything involving blood or doctors, even a small cut on my hand can trigger it now.”
D012-D018_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h002.question: "I’m here because of these panic attacks, especially whenever I get into tight spaces. It started after that structural collapse last year; we were trapped in the debris for hours. Now, if I even think about going into an attic during a search, or even a small crawlspace, my heart starts pounding, I can't breathe, and I get dizzy. It’s been happening for about eight months now. It's really affecting my job. My wife and I even had to postpone our vacation because I just can't deal with the idea of getting on a plane, let alone a cramped subway. It's not like I'm reliving the collapse or constantly thinking about it, just the enclosed spaces themselves trigger this extreme fear. I just want to be able to do my job without feeling like I'm going to lose control."
D012-D018_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h003.question: It's all gotten rather debilitating, doctor. For the past year, it's been this intense fear of vomiting.  Initially, I thought it was just a bad bout of food poisoning that triggered it, but it’s become so much more. I used to enjoy dining out with my wife, but now the thought of anyone around me getting sick, even a child, sends me into a full-blown panic. I’m constantly on edge, checking exits in restaurants, always aware of where the restrooms are. Sometimes, if I even hear someone cough a certain way, I just freeze up completely. My mind goes blank, and I feel completely paralyzed, unable to move or think. It’s hard to explain, but it’s not that I’m reliving the food poisoning; I’m just terrified of the vomiting itself and what might lead to it. It’s affecting my lectures, too. I find myself scanning the lecture hall, worried about a student suddenly becoming unwell.
D012-D018_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h004.question: "Well, I'm 57, a civil engineer, and lately, things have just felt… off. It all started after that bridge collapse I witnessed about seven months ago. The sheer chaos, the noise, the feeling of helplessness… I was on site, overseeing a new construction nearby. Ever since then, I get this overwhelming fear whenever I have to go through tunnels or cross bridges. It’s instantaneous; the moment I see one, my heart races, palms sweat, and I just feel this urge to run. It's really affecting my work; my commute has become a nightmare. I’ve tried to just power through it, but the panic is too intense. I haven't been able to eat properly, have trouble sleeping, and I'm constantly on edge, but it's really the bridges and tunnels that trigger me most directly. I just can't seem to shake that feeling of terror."
D012-D018_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h005.question:
(Sighs, picking at a loose thread on her sweater)

It’s been about eight months now, ever since… that day at work. I was grooming a dog, and another groomer accidentally cut herself pretty badly. There was blood everywhere, and I just… stopped. I couldn't move. My mind went blank, and I felt completely frozen. It was terrifying. Now, even the thought of seeing blood, or getting a shot at the doctor, makes my heart race. I avoid the vet’s office unless I absolutely have to, and I get so anxious even thinking about a routine check-up. That whole incident was awful, but honestly, it’s not something I constantly relive or have nightmares about. It was just a really bad experience that’s left me with this overwhelming fear of blood and needles.
D012-D018_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h006.question: "Lately, I've just been… on edge. It’s hard to even pinpoint when it started, but even thinking about blood, needles, or medical procedures now sends me into a full-blown panic. My heart starts pounding like I’ve just run a marathon, I can't catch my breath, and I get all sweaty and shaky. It’s a pretty big problem for a paramedic, as you can imagine. I’ve had to push through it on calls, trying to keep it together while someone’s bleeding out or needs an IV, but it’s pure agony and I'm terrified I'll mess up. It’s weird because I’ve seen some pretty awful things on the job, one really bad accident a few months ago… but it’s not really *that* that haunts me. It’s always the blood or the needles that get me, and other than that specific fear, I’d say I’ve been doing okay since the accident. I’m sleeping fine, no nightmares or flashbacks, and I’m not avoiding other things related to the job or isolating myself. It’s just this intense fear of blood and injuries that's really bothering me and affecting my work.”
D012-D018_h006.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h007.question: "Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It's… tough to talk about. A couple of months ago, I was in a bad accident at the restaurant, cut my hand pretty deep. Saw a lot of blood. Ever since then, it’s been… different. Just the sight of blood, even a little scratch, makes my heart pound, my chest tight, and I start shaking uncontrollably. It’s like all the air gets sucked out of the room. I’ve started going to extremes to avoid anything that might involve blood. I’m usually so hands-on, but now I’m constantly delegating prep work, even things like butchering meat, which I used to love. I even avoid watching medical shows with my son. I know it sounds crazy, and the accident itself wasn't good, but apart from this fear, I'm sleeping fine, no nightmares or flashing back to it, and I'm not feeling detached or constantly on edge because of it. It’s just this intense, immediate panic whenever blood is in sight."
D012-D018_h007.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h008.question: "It's been a tough year, doctor. Ever since that incident six months ago – I was hiking, and a dog, off-leash, just went for my leg. Didn't break the skin, thankfully, but it really shook me up. Now, anything to do with dogs sends me into a tailspin. If I even see a picture of a dog, or hear one bark down the street, my heart starts racing, and I get this overwhelming sense of dread. My friends keep inviting me to their backyard BBQs, but I always make an excuse. I’ve even started taking a longer route to work to avoid a park where people walk their dogs, even though it adds twenty minutes to my commute. It’s definitely impacting me, but it’s just the dogs. I'm not having nightmares or flashbacks about the event itself, and it’s not like I’m constantly on edge or avoiding all social situations. It's really just the dogs, and that intense fear they stir up."
D012-D018_h008.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h009.question: It's been hard to even think about going to work these past few months. I'm an art restorer, and a few months ago, a bat flew into the studio through an open window. Of course, it startled everyone, and I was really scared, but I've been a wreck ever since. Even seeing pictures of them, or hearing something about bats on TV, makes my heart pound and leaves me feeling shaky. I know it's probably silly; I try to tell myself it was just a bat, and it's over, but the fear just consumes me. My husband suggested we go camping last weekend, and even though I knew the chances of seeing a bat were slim, I just couldn't bring myself to go. My body was tense with anxiety the whole time I pictured it. I'm embarrassed to admit it, but sometimes I still replay that day in my head, feeling that same surge of panic. It's impacting my ability to concentrate on my delicate work.
D012-D018_h009.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h010.question: "It’s mostly been about five months now, Doctor, since that huge storm hit. I was driving home, and the rain was just… relentless, truly terrifying. Since then, I can’t handle even a dark, cloudy sky. Seeing any sign of a storm brewing sends me into a full-blown panic. My heart starts pounding, I can’t catch my breath, and I get so shaky and sweaty, it’s just awful. I’ve started checking the weather obsessively, and if there’s even a slight chance of rain or thunder, I'll rearrange my entire day to avoid going outside. I’ve missed classes and even skipped a few study group meetings because of it. I know it sounds silly, but I'm constantly on edge. It feels like this fear started after that one really bad storm, but honestly, besides that initial scare, I don't really dwell on it or have nightmares or flashbacks. It’s just this intense fear of storms now."
D012-D018_h010.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D012-D018_h011.question: "It’s gotten to the point where I just can’t relax anymore, doctor. This has been going on for over seven months now. My divorce was rough, and after that awful mugging in the park where that dog bit me, I just haven't been the same. Every time I see a dog, any dog, my heart starts pounding, I get dizzy, and I just *need* to get away. I know it sounds irrational, but I genuinely feel threatened. I can only manage to walk outside if my son is with me, or if I carry my heavy walking stick, like some kind of security blanket. The thought of encountering one sends shivers down my spine. It’s not like I’m reliving the mugging itself over and over, though. I just dread running into another dog."
D012-D018_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h012.question: It started after *the incident* a few months ago – that terrible storm where the tree fell right outside my apartment. Now, whenever the sky darkens, or I hear even a distant rumble of thunder, I feel this absolute dread. I know, logically, that most storms aren't dangerous, but I can't shake the overwhelming panic. I try to distract myself, burying myself in my PhD work, but my heart races, and my breathing gets shallow. Last week, I had a presentation, and a storm rolled in right as I was about to leave. I felt physically sick with fear, but I forced myself into the downpour because I absolutely couldn't miss it. Every drop of rain felt like a threat. It’s not like I’m constantly reliving the event itself, or having nightmares, but the *fear* of storms has just completely taken over.
D012-D018_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h013.question: It's gotten so bad lately, I'm almost ashamed to talk about it, being a fitness trainer and all. Lately, just the thought of seeing blood – even a tiny cut – sends me into a full-blown panic. I almost passed out just watching a documentary about surgery the other day, my heart was racing, and I felt lightheaded. I avoid anything medical-related like the plague now. I had a really nasty accident about five months ago, broke my arm pretty badly and there was a lot of blood, and the whole hospital experience was awful. Now, if I even have to go to a doctor's office, I pretty much demand my buddy comes with me just so I have someone to hold onto or distract me. I know it sounds ridiculous because it’s not like anything else from the accident really bothers me anymore, but the sight of blood… that’s another story.
D012-D018_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h014.question: "Lately, I’ve been dreading my shifts more and more. It’s the tunnels, mostly. The darkness, how long they stretch out… sometimes I feel like the walls are closing in. I’ll white-knuckle the controls, sweating, just trying to get through it. I have this lucky keychain, a little train car, and I'll grip it hard the whole time, almost like it's protecting me. I know it sounds crazy, but it helps a little. This started after that pile-up about six months ago, the one where the train ahead lost power in the tunnel. I wasn't directly involved, but seeing all that chaos, being so close... it really shook me up. I had a few nightmares about it right after, and I'd jump at loud noises for a bit, but that all mostly calmed down after a few weeks. Now it's just this intense fear of the tunnels themselves. My buddies think I'm going soft, but I can't help it. I even try to swap shifts to avoid the routes with the longer underground sections. It’s definitely messing with my head, and my job."
D012-D018_h014.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h015.question: "It all started after that terrible car accident two years ago. I was trapped in my car for what felt like an eternity before the paramedics got to me. Now, any time I'm in a tight space, especially elevators or even just really crowded rooms, I feel this overwhelming panic. My heart starts racing, I get lightheaded, and I just *need* to get out. My husband usually has to come with me if we’re going anywhere with an elevator, and I basically hold onto his arm for dear life the whole time. It's gotten to the point where I'll take the stairs no matter how many flights, which is a real problem at work sometimes, considering I’m a speech therapist in a big hospital. The accident was awful, but honestly, I don't really have nightmares about it anymore or keep replaying it in my head. It's just the enclosed spaces that really get to me."
D012-D018_h015.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D012-D018_h016.question: I’m here because… well, it’s been a good few months now, close to a year actually, since the accident. That pile-up in the tunnel was horrific. I was lucky to walk away, really, but ever since, I just can’t do tunnels. Or bridges, for that matter. Even thinking about driving into one makes my heart pound and my hands sweat. I get this sickening dread. It's gotten so bad I've changed my entire route to work, even if it means a significantly longer commute. My ex-husband keeps telling me to just "get over it," but he doesn't understand. I do try, sometimes, if there's absolutely no other way. I white-knuckle the steering wheel, barely breathing, feeling like the walls are closing in, just desperate for it to be over. But it’s not just the direct memory of the crash that haunts me; it's this overwhelming terror of being *in* another tunnel. It’s hard to even enjoy my grandkids, because I’m so jumpy and on edge all the time. But I don't replay the accident in my head constantly, I don't have nightmares, or feel detached from everyone like some people describe for PTSD. It's really just the tunnels themselves, and the bridges, that get me.
D012-D018_h016.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h017.question: "Thanks for seeing me, Doc. It’s been… a rough few months, probably since that whole incident at the factory, when that new machine jammed with all that awful grinding and banging. I thought someone was seriously hurt. Now, anytime I hear a sudden, loud noise, especially anything mechanical, my heart just starts pounding out of my chest. I get clammy, start sweating, and feel like I can’t catch my breath. It's ridiculous, I know, but I actually go out of my way to avoid the production floor now, even if it means delegating tasks I should be doing myself as supervisor. It's not like that one event replay in my head, or I keep reliving it; it’s more just the sounds. I just can't stand those loud, unexpected noises anymore."
D012-D018_h017.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h018.question: "Thank you for seeing me, Doctor. Lately, things have been really tough, especially with my work in real estate. The big issue for me is seeing blood, even a little scratch on a client... or if I get a papercut myself. My heart pounds, my vision tunnels, and I just freeze up. It's like my body entirely locks up, and I can't move or speak. I remember a few months ago, I witnessed a pretty bad car accident on my way to a showing – lots of blood. It was horrifying. Ever since then, this fear has been so much worse. I know it sounds silly, but I'll literally cross the street to avoid construction sites where there might be exposed rebar, just in case. And when I have to go for my annual check-ups, even the thought of a needle makes me sick. I usually force myself to go because I have to, but I'm just a wreck the whole time, shaking and holding back tears. It’s been constant. However, apart from that one incident, I don't really have nightmares or feel keyed up all the time like some people do after something traumatic. It's really just the blood and injuries that get to me."
D012-D018_h018.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h019.question: "It all started after the accident, you know, when my ex-husband's car hit that deer. I mean, I wasn't hurt, but ever since then, if I even *see* a deer, let alone hear anything about them, I just freeze. My heart races like crazy, I can't catch my breath, and my hands start trembling so bad I can’t hold anything. I know it sounds silly, being a grown woman and all, but I swear I feel like I'm going to pass out. I try to avoid driving on rural roads now, and if I absolutely have to, I make sure my friend is with me in the car. It’s like I need someone there to calm me down if something happens. Even though that car crash was awful, I don't really have nightmares about it or feel constantly on edge like some people describe. It's just... the deer. Just the deer."
D012-D018_h019.options:
A. Binge-Eating Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h020.question: It’s gotten to the point where I dread going out. The thought of encountering a loud, sudden noise, like a car backfiring or a balloon popping, sends shivers down my spine. I was in a minor car accident a few months ago – just a fender bender, really – but the sound of the impact really rattled me. I try to avoid busy streets, and if I have to go to a crowded area, I practically cling to my friend’s arm the whole time. It's been this way for about four months now. I know it sounds silly, and the accident itself wasn't a huge ordeal, but this fear… it’s just consumed me.

    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia

D012-D018_h021.question: "It all started after that terrible car accident three years ago. I was trapped for hours, felt like forever, in the wreckage. Now, I can’t even fathom getting into an enclosed space. Tunnels are a nightmare; every time my husband drives near one, my heart starts racing and I get this horrible sense of dread. Even elevators at work, which is pretty inconvenient in my line of work, feel like death traps. I try to avoid them, but sometimes, for client meetings on higher floors, I just have to force myself. I’m visibly shaking and sweating the whole time, gripping the railing until my knuckles are white, just trying to get through it. It's not like I'm having flashbacks or anything, I just feel this intense, overwhelming panic specifically about being in those tight spaces. It's really affecting my job, since a lot of my clients are in high-rise offices, and I find myself making excuses not to go."
D012-D018_h021.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h022.question: "It's mainly the storms, doctor. After that tornado hit out of nowhere last year, I just haven't been the same. Every time the sky darkens or the wind picks up, my heart races, I start sweating, and I can barely breathe. Even checking the weather forecast sends me into a panic. I try to tough it out, but I'm just a wreck until it passes. I did go through a pretty intense time with a lot of flashbacks and nightmares right after the tornado and when my house was damaged, but that's mostly settled down now. It's just this fear of storms that lingers, even though I'm not reliving the whole thing anymore like I used to."
D012-D018_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D018_h023.question: It’s been about a year since that accident on the site – a beam fell, not on me, thankfully, but I saw the whole thing, the blood, the bone… ever since then, I can hardly stand the sight of any blood, even a cut finger.
